# Glossary

| Term | Definition | Lesson | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Florida Statutes (F.S.) | Laws passed by the Florida Legislature, organized by chapter and section (e.g., s. 475.25). | L01-1 |  |
| Chapter 475, F.S. | Florida's real estate license law: brokers, sales associates, schools, appraisers (Part II). | L01-1 |  |
| Chapter 455, F.S. | General law for all professions regulated by the DBPR (applications, investigations, discipline procedures). | L01-1 |  |
| Florida Administrative Code (F.A.C.) | Rules adopted by state agencies under authority given by a statute. FREC's rules are Chapter 61J2. | L01-1 | A rule has the force of law but must stay within its statute. |
| Rule 61J2 | The FREC's rule chapter in the Florida Administrative Code (escrow, advertising, education, offices). | L01-1 |  |
| Case law | Law made by court decisions that interpret statutes or develop common law; e.g., Johnson v. Davis (seller must disclose known latent defects). | L01-1 | Florida (like most of the US) is a common-law system; Portugal is a civil-law system. |
| Common law | Legal rules developed by courts over time, rather than written in a code. | L01-1 |  |
| FREC | Florida Real Estate Commission: 7 members appointed by the Governor; makes rules and disciplines licensees. | L01-1 |  |
| DBPR | Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation; its Division of Real Estate provides FREC's administrative services, issues licenses and investigates complaints. | L01-1 |  |
| Real estate | Land plus everything permanently attached to it (improvements), and the rights that go with ownership. | L01-2 |  |
| Real property | Real estate together with the bundle of legal rights of ownership. | L01-2 |  |
| Personal property | Movable items not attached to land (chattels); co-op shares are personal property. | L01-2 |  |
| REALTOR® | A registered trademark identifying members of the National Association of REALTORS® (NAR), who agree to its Code of Ethics. | L01-2 | Not a license. A licensee need not be a REALTOR®. |
| NAR | National Association of REALTORS®, the largest US trade association for real estate professionals. | L01-2 |  |
| Realtist | Member of the National Association of Real Estate Brokers (NAREB). | L01-2 |  |
| Property management | Specialty of managing property for owners: leasing, rent collection, maintenance. | L01-2 |  |
| Special-purpose property | Property with a unique use, such as churches, schools, hospitals. | L01-2 |  |
| Sales associate | Person licensed to perform real estate services for compensation, but only under the direction of an employing broker or owner-developer. | L02-1 | Florida term for what other states call a salesperson. |
| Broker | Person licensed to perform real estate services for others for compensation in their own name; may open an office and hold escrow. | L02-1 |  |
| Broker associate | A person with a broker license who chooses to work under another broker. | L03-2 |  |
| Compensation | Anything of value — money, gifts, property — paid or promised, or even expected, for a real estate service. | L02-1 |  |
| Attorney in fact | Person authorized by a power of attorney to sign for another; exempt only for executing contracts or conveyances. | L02-2 | Not the same as an attorney at law (lawyer). |
| Nolo contendere | Plea of 'no contest': the defendant does not admit guilt but accepts the penalty. Must be reported within 30 days like a guilty plea. | L03-4 |  |
| Mutual recognition | Agreement letting nonresident licensees of certain states obtain a Florida license by passing a 40-question Florida law exam. | L02-3 | Not 'reciprocity' — the exam uses the precise term. |
| Quasi-legislative | Rule-making power exercised by an agency (FREC adopting 61J2 rules). | L03-1 |  |
| Quasi-judicial | Power of an agency to decide disputes and impose discipline (FREC final orders). | L03-1 |  |
| Registration | Recording a licensee's name, address, employer and status in DBPR records. | L03-2 |  |
| Licensure | DBPR's certification that a person has met the qualifications to hold a license. | L03-2 |  |
| Group license | Registration allowing a sales associate to work for several connected entities of one owner-developer. | L03-2 |  |
| Multiple licenses | Separate licenses a BROKER may hold for separate, unconnected brokerages. | L03-2 | Sales associates cannot hold multiple licenses. |
| Active license | License whose holder is registered with an employing broker (or, for a broker, an office) and may practice. | L03-3 |  |
| Voluntary inactive | Status chosen by the licensee; may be renewed indefinitely with CE. | L03-3 |  |
| Involuntary inactive | Status caused by failure to renew; expires (void) after 2 years. | L03-3 |  |
| Null and void | The license has ceased to exist; the person must requalify. | L03-3 |  |
| Ineffective license | A license that exists but cannot be used, e.g., a sales associate with no employing broker. | L03-4 |  |
| Post-licensing education | 45-hour course a sales associate must complete before the first renewal. | L03-3 |  |
| Continuing education (CE) | 14 hours every 2-year renewal period after the first: 3 Core Law + 3 Ethics and Business Practices + 8 specialty. | L03-3 |  |
| Transaction broker | A licensee providing limited representation to a buyer, seller or both; not a fiduciary. Presumed in Florida. | L04-1 |  |
| Single agent | A broker who represents one party (the principal) as a fiduciary. | L04-1 |  |
| No brokerage relationship | A licensee works with a party without representing them; owes 3 duties. | L04-1 |  |
| Dual agency | Acting as fiduciary agent for both buyer and seller in one transaction; prohibited in Florida. | L04-1 |  |
| Fiduciary | A person in a relationship of trust who must put the principal's interests first. | L04-1 |  |
| Principal | The person a single agent represents. | L04-1 |  |
| Customer | A party a licensee works with but does not represent as a fiduciary. | L04-1 |  |
| Limited confidentiality | Transaction-broker duty not to reveal that the seller will accept less, the buyer will pay more, a party's motivation, or other information a party asks to keep confidential. | L04-2 |  |
| Consent to Transition | Signed consent of a principal allowing the single agent to become a transaction broker. | L04-3 |  |
| Residential sale | Sale of ≤4 residential units, unimproved land for ≤4 units, or agricultural property ≤10 acres. | L04-3 |  |
| Material fact | A fact that would affect a reasonable person's decision or the property's value. | L04-4 |  |
| Latent defect | A hidden defect not discoverable by ordinary inspection. | L04-4 |  |
| Designated sales associate | Associate appointed as single agent for one party in a nonresidential deal where each party has $1M+ in assets. | L04-4 |  |
| Escrow (trust) account | Account holding money belonging to others (deposits, rents). | L05-1 |  |
| Earnest money / binder deposit | Deposit a buyer gives to show good faith, usually held in escrow. | L05-1 | Not the Portuguese 'sinal' — no automatic double-return rule. |
| Commingling | Mixing personal or business funds with escrow funds. | L05-1 |  |
| Conversion | Using escrow funds for personal or unauthorized purposes. | L05-1 |  |
| Escrow Disbursement Order (EDO) | Order from FREC deciding who receives disputed escrow funds held by a broker. | L05-2 |  |
| Interpleader | Lawsuit in which the broker deposits disputed funds with the court and asks it to decide who is entitled. | L05-2 |  |
| Mediation | Non-binding process with a neutral third party; requires all parties' written consent. | L05-2 |  |
| Arbitration | Binding decision by a neutral arbitrator; requires all parties' consent. | L05-2 |  |
| Blind ad | Advertisement that fails to include the brokerage's registered name. | L05-3 |  |
| Kickback | Payment for referring business; restricted by Chapter 475 and prohibited by RESPA in most residential financed deals. | L05-4 |  |
| Price fixing | Competitors agreeing on commission rates; illegal under antitrust law. | L05-4 |  |
| Branch office | Additional location where the broker conducts business; must be registered. | L05-4 |  |
| Legally sufficient complaint | A complaint alleging facts that, if true, would violate a statute or rule. | L06-1 |  |
| Probable cause panel | Panel that decides whether the investigation supports filing a formal complaint. | L06-1 |  |
| Administrative law judge (ALJ) | Judge from the Division of Administrative Hearings who conducts formal hearings and recommends an order. | L06-1 |  |
| Final order | FREC's decision on discipline. | L06-1 |  |
| Citation | Fixed fine for a listed minor violation, offered instead of formal proceedings. | L06-2 |  |
| Notice of noncompliance | Written notice for a first minor violation, letting the licensee correct it. | L06-2 |  |
| Culpable negligence | Reckless indifference to others' rights — more than simple carelessness. | L06-2 |  |
| Misrepresentation | False statement or concealment of a material fact. | L06-2 |  |
| Real Estate Recovery Fund | State fund that pays consumers who cannot collect a judgment against a licensee arising from a brokerage transaction. | L06-3 |  |
| Steering | Directing buyers or renters toward or away from areas based on a protected class. | L07-1 |  |
| Blockbusting (panic peddling) | Inducing owners to sell by suggesting a protected class is moving in. | L07-1 |  |
| Redlining | A lender refusing loans or changing terms in certain areas for discriminatory reasons. | L07-1 |  |
| Familial status | Households with children under 18, pregnant women, or people obtaining custody. | L07-1 |  |
| Reasonable modification | Physical change to a unit for a person with a disability, generally at the tenant's expense. | L07-1 |  |
| Reasonable accommodation | Change in rules or policies for a person with a disability (e.g., assistance animal despite a no-pets rule). | L07-1 |  |
| RESPA | Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act: closing disclosures and anti-kickback rules for federally related residential loans. | L07-3 |  |
| TILA / Regulation Z | Truth in Lending Act: disclosure of credit costs, APR, advertising trigger terms, right of rescission. | L07-3 |  |
| APR | Annual percentage rate: the yearly cost of credit including interest and certain fees. | L07-3 |  |
| Trigger term | Specific credit term in an ad (down payment amount, payment amount, number of payments, finance charge) that requires full disclosure. | L07-3 |  |
| TRID | TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure. | L07-3 |  |
| ECOA | Equal Credit Opportunity Act: no credit discrimination by race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (if able to contract), public assistance income, or good-faith exercise of consumer credit rights. | L07-2 |  |
| ADA | Americans with Disabilities Act: accessibility of public accommodations and commercial facilities. | L07-2 |  |
| HMDA | Home Mortgage Disclosure Act: lenders report lending data that reveals patterns like redlining. | L07-2 |  |
| Bundle of rights | Ownership rights: possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition. | L08-1 |  |
| Freehold estate | Ownership of indeterminate duration (fee simple, life estate). | L08-1 |  |
| Fee simple absolute | The most complete ownership, inheritable and unconditional. | L08-1 |  |
| Fee simple defeasible | Ownership that can be lost if a stated condition occurs or is breached. | L08-1 |  |
| Life estate | Ownership limited to the life of a person. | L08-1 | Similar in purpose to usufruto, but a distinct legal form. |
| Pur autre vie | Life estate measured by the life of someone other than the life tenant. | L08-1 |  |
| Remainder / remainderman | Future interest passing to a third party when a life estate ends. | L08-1 |  |
| Reversion | Future interest returning to the grantor (or heirs) when a life estate ends. | L08-1 |  |
| Waste | Damage or neglect by a life tenant that harms the future interest. | L08-1 |  |
| Leasehold (nonfreehold) estate | Right of possession under a lease, without ownership. | L08-2 |  |
| Estate for years | Lease for a fixed term (any length); ends without notice. | L08-2 |  |
| Periodic tenancy | Lease renewing period to period (week, month, quarter, year) until notice. | L08-2 |  |
| Tenancy at will | Tenancy of indefinite duration terminable by proper notice. | L08-2 |  |
| Tenancy at sufferance | Holdover tenant who stays without the landlord's consent. | L08-2 |  |
| Gross lease | Tenant pays fixed rent; landlord pays operating expenses. | L08-2 |  |
| Net lease | Tenant pays rent plus some or all property expenses (triple net: taxes, insurance, maintenance). | L08-2 |  |
| Percentage lease | Rent includes a percentage of the tenant's gross sales, usually above a base rent. | L08-2 |  |
| Ground lease | Long-term lease of land on which the tenant builds. | L08-2 |  |
| Assignment | Transfer of the ENTIRE remaining lease term. | L08-2 |  |
| Sublease | Transfer of part of the remaining term or part of the space. | L08-2 |  |
| Tenancy in common | Co-ownership with undivided, possibly unequal shares and no survivorship. | L08-3 |  |
| Joint tenancy with right of survivorship | Co-ownership with the four unities; deceased owner's share passes to survivors. | L08-3 |  |
| Tenancy by the entireties | Ownership by a married couple as one unit; survivorship; protected from one spouse's creditors. | L08-3 |  |
| PITT (four unities) | Possession, Interest, Time, Title. | L08-3 |  |
| Partition | Court action to divide co-owned property or force its sale. | L08-3 |  |
| Homestead | A Florida owner's primary residence, with creditor protection, transfer restrictions, and tax exemption. | L08-4 |  |
| Condominium | Ownership of a unit in fee simple plus an undivided share of common elements, created by a recorded declaration. | L08-5 |  |
| Common elements | Parts of a condominium owned in common (lobby, pool, roof). | L08-5 |  |
| Cooperative | A corporation owns the building; residents own shares and hold proprietary leases (personal property). | L08-5 |  |
| Proprietary lease | Lease giving a co-op shareholder the right to occupy a unit. | L08-5 |  |
| Timeshare | Right to use a unit for a set period each year. | L08-5 |  |
| HOA | Homeowners' association: mandatory-membership community governed by recorded covenants. | L08-5 |  |
| CDD | Community Development District: special-purpose local government that finances community infrastructure through assessments. | L08-5 |  |
| Title | Ownership and the evidence of it. | L09-1 |  |
| Escheat | Property passing to the state when an owner dies without a will or heirs. | L09-1 |  |
| Eminent domain | Government's power to take private property for public use with just compensation (condemnation). | L09-1 |  |
| Adverse possession | Acquiring title by open, notorious, hostile, continuous possession for 7 years in Florida plus color of title or payment of taxes. | L09-1 |  |
| Color of title | A document that appears to give title but is defective. | L09-1 |  |
| Testate / intestate | Dying with / without a valid will. | L09-1 |  |
| Devise / devisee | Gift of real property by will / its recipient. | L09-1 |  |
| Descent | Transfer of an intestate's property to heirs under statute. | L09-1 |  |
| Grantor / grantee | The person conveying / receiving title by deed. | L09-2 |  |
| General warranty deed | Grantor warrants title against defects from any time. | L09-2 |  |
| Special warranty deed | Grantor warrants only against defects arising during their ownership. | L09-2 |  |
| Bargain and sale deed | Implies the grantor owns the property but gives no warranties. | L09-2 |  |
| Quitclaim deed | Conveys whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranties. | L09-2 |  |
| Cloud on title | A claim or defect that impairs title. | L09-2 |  |
| Acknowledgment | Formal declaration before a notary that the signer signed voluntarily; needed to record. | L09-2 |  |
| Seisin | Covenant that the grantor owns the property and has the right to convey it. | L09-2 |  |
| Constructive notice | Notice the law presumes from public records or visible possession. | L09-3 |  |
| Actual notice | What a person actually knows. | L09-3 |  |
| Abstract of title | Summary of all recorded documents affecting a property's title. | L09-3 |  |
| Title insurance | Policy protecting against losses from title defects existing before the policy date. | L09-3 |  |
| Encumbrance | Any claim or limitation on title (lien, easement, restriction, encroachment). | L09-4 |  |
| Lien | A claim against property as security for a debt. | L09-4 |  |
| Specific lien | Lien on one property (mortgage, property tax, construction lien). | L09-4 |  |
| General lien | Lien on all the debtor's property (judgment, IRS lien). | L09-4 |  |
| Subordination | A lienholder agreeing to a lower priority. | L09-4 |  |
| Easement appurtenant | Easement benefiting an adjoining parcel (dominant) over a burdened parcel (servient); runs with the land. | L09-4 |  |
| Easement in gross | Easement benefiting a person or company (e.g., utility), not a parcel. | L09-4 |  |
| Easement by prescription | Easement acquired by 20 years of open, continuous, adverse use in Florida. | L09-4 |  |
| License (land use) | Revocable personal permission to use land; not an interest in land. | L09-4 | Different meaning from a real estate license. |
| Encroachment | A structure or improvement extending onto another's land. | L09-4 |  |
| Deed restriction (restrictive covenant) | Private limitation on use recorded in a deed or plat. | L09-4 |  |
| Fixture | Personal property attached to real property so that it becomes part of it. | L09-5 |  |
| Trade fixture | Item a business tenant installs for its trade; remains the tenant's personal property. | L09-5 |  |
| Emblements | Annual crops produced by labor; personal property. | L09-5 |  |
| Riparian rights | Rights of owners along rivers and streams. | L09-5 |  |
| Littoral rights | Rights of owners along oceans, seas and large lakes. | L09-5 |  |
| Accretion / avulsion | Gradual addition of land by water deposits (owner gains) / sudden loss or change (boundary does not move). | L09-5 |  |
| Metes and bounds | Description using a point of beginning, directions (courses) and distances, returning to the POB. | L10-1 |  |
| Point of beginning (POB) | Starting and ending point of a metes-and-bounds description. | L10-1 |  |
| Lot and block | Description by lot and block numbers on a recorded plat. | L10-1 |  |
| Plat | Recorded map of a subdivision. | L10-1 |  |
| Government (rectangular) survey | System of townships and sections measured from principal meridians and base lines. | L10-1 |  |
| Township | 6 × 6 mile square, 36 sections. | L10-2 |  |
| Section | 1 square mile, 640 acres. | L10-2 |  |
| Front foot | A foot of frontage along a street or water; the first dimension given. | L14-2 |  |
| Bilateral contract | Promise for a promise (e.g., sale contract). | L11-1 |  |
| Unilateral contract | Promise for an act (e.g., option, reward). | L11-1 |  |
| Executory / executed | Obligations still to perform / fully performed. | L11-1 |  |
| Void / voidable / unenforceable | No contract at all / one party may cancel / valid but courts won't enforce. | L11-1 |  |
| Statute of frauds | Law requiring certain contracts (sale of real estate, >1 year) to be written and signed. | L11-1 |  |
| Consideration | Something of value exchanged; mutual promises suffice. | L11-1 |  |
| Counteroffer | A response that changes the terms; it rejects and terminates the original offer. | L11-2 |  |
| Option | Contract giving the optionee the right to buy at set terms during a period; optionor is bound. | L11-2 |  |
| Equitable title | Buyer's interest under a signed sale contract before closing. | L11-2 |  |
| Specific performance | Court order to perform the contract as agreed. | L11-2 |  |
| Liquidated damages | Damages agreed in advance (often the deposit). | L11-2 |  |
| Procuring cause | The broker whose efforts started an uninterrupted chain of events leading to the sale. | L11-3 |  |
| Open listing | Listing given to several brokers; only the procuring broker is paid; owner may sell free. | L11-3 |  |
| Exclusive agency listing | One brokerage; owner keeps the right to sell without commission. | L11-3 |  |
| Exclusive right of sale | One brokerage earns the commission no matter who sells. | L11-3 |  |
| Net listing | Broker keeps any amount above the seller's net price. | L11-3 |  |
| Effective date | Date the last party signs or initials the final offer/counteroffer and it is communicated; contract deadlines run from it. | L11-4 |  |
| Time is of the essence | Clause making contract deadlines strict. | L11-4 |  |
| AS IS contract | Seller makes no repairs; buyer may inspect and cancel within the inspection period. | L11-4 |  |
| Promissory note | The borrower's written promise to repay the debt. | L12-1 |  |
| Mortgage | Security instrument pledging property for a debt. | L12-1 | In US usage 'mortgage' is the document, not the loan. |
| Mortgagor / mortgagee | Borrower (gives the mortgage) / lender (receives it). | L12-1 |  |
| Lien theory | The borrower keeps title; the lender holds a lien (Florida). | L12-1 |  |
| Acceleration clause | Lets the lender demand the entire balance on default. | L12-1 |  |
| Due-on-sale (alienation) clause | Balance becomes due if the property is transferred. | L12-1 |  |
| Defeasance clause | The mortgage is defeated (cancelled) when the debt is paid. | L12-1 |  |
| Exculpatory clause | Borrower not personally liable; lender looks only to the property. | L12-1 |  |
| Assumption | Buyer takes over the loan and becomes personally liable. | L12-2 |  |
| Novation | Substitution of a new party that releases the original borrower. | L12-2 |  |
| Subject to | Buyer takes title and pays the loan without personal liability. | L12-2 |  |
| Equity of redemption | Borrower's right to pay off the debt and stop foreclosure until the sale. | L12-2 |  |
| Deficiency judgment | Judgment for the unpaid balance after a foreclosure sale. | L12-2 |  |
| Short sale | Sale where the lender accepts less than the amount owed. | L12-2 |  |
| Deed in lieu of foreclosure | Borrower deeds the property to the lender to avoid foreclosure; junior liens survive. | L12-2 |  |
| PITI | Principal, interest, taxes, insurance — the monthly housing payment. | L12-3 |  |
| Usury | Charging interest above the legal maximum. | L12-3 |  |
| LTV | Loan-to-value ratio: loan ÷ lesser of price or appraised value. | L14-5 |  |
| FHA | Federal Housing Administration (HUD): insures loans; borrower pays MIP. | L13-1 |  |
| VA | Department of Veterans Affairs: guarantees loans to eligible veterans. | L13-1 |  |
| PMI | Private mortgage insurance on conventional loans above 80% LTV. | L13-1 |  |
| Amortized loan | Level payments covering interest and principal until fully repaid. | L13-2 |  |
| Balloon payment | Large final payment on a partially amortized loan. | L13-2 |  |
| ARM | Adjustable-rate mortgage: rate = index + margin, limited by caps. | L13-2 |  |
| Package mortgage | Covers real and personal property. | L13-2 |  |
| Blanket mortgage | Covers several parcels; release clause frees parcels as paid. | L13-2 |  |
| Wraparound mortgage | New junior loan that includes an existing loan. | L13-2 |  |
| Purchase-money mortgage | Seller finances part of the price. | L13-2 |  |

| Primary market | Lenders who originate loans. | L13-3 |  |

| Proration | Dividing an expense or income between buyer and seller as of closing. | L14-7 |  |

| In advance | Paid at the start of the period (rent, insurance premiums). | L14-7 |  |
| Debit | An amount a party owes at closing. | L14-8 |  |
| Credit | An amount a party receives at closing. | L14-8 |  |

| Intangible tax | Florida one-time tax of 2 mills on new mortgages. | L14-6 |  |
| CMA | Comparative market analysis by a licensee to suggest a price range. | L15-1 |  |
| BPO | Broker price opinion, often for lenders; chargeable but not an appraisal. | L15-1 |  |
